Explain and practise: Number Palindrome

Study exercise derived from this source. Explain the approach in your own words, work through an example, and identify edge cases. For code, implement your own version and discuss its time and space complexity.

Original source context
# Number Palindrome

George and  Tintin plays  by  telling numbers.  George says a number to Tintin.  Tintin should first reverse the number and check if it is same as the original.  If yes,  Tintin should say “Palindrome”.  If not, he should say “Not a Palindrome”.  If the number is negative, print “Invalid Input”.  Help Tintin by writing a program.

> Sample Input 1 :

    21212

> Sample Output 1 :

    Palindrome


> Sample Input 2 :

    6186

> Sample Output 2 :

    Not a Palindrome
